sources.title: Development Document for Effluent Limitations Guidelines and Standards of Performance: The Clay, Gypsum, Refractory and Ceramic Products Industries
sources.version_or_release: April 1975; Draft contractor report; Contract No. 68-01-2633. Cover explicitly says not an official EPA publication and not reviewed by EPA.
sources.locator: Section V §3.7.2 pp. V-64–65; §§3.7.4–3.7.5 pp. V-67–68; Section VII §§2.1, 1.0, 1.5 pp. VII-1–4; Section VIII pp. VIII-23–24.
sources.observed_operation: Surveyed pottery plants had variable clay/glaze-bearing wastes and intermittent small flows; reported one small art pottery recycling after settling, multiple settling/flocculation practices, and one complex plant filtering underflows, recycling filtrate, and landfilling filter cake.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Historical draft evidence only. It states fine clays may remain after settling, performance varies with solids and basin configuration, glaze formulations affect metal concerns, and some records lacked metals analyses. It is not current law or a reviewed EPA finding.
sources.applicability: Mechanism and historical implementation context; industrial and dated evidence cannot establish current local permission, small-shop efficacy, dissolved-phase removal, or a solids route.

sources.title: eCFR 40 CFR §403.5 — National pretreatment standards: Prohibited discharges
sources.version_or_release: Current eCFR page as of 2026-10-07; page states Title 40 last amended 2026-10-02.
sources.observed_operation: General pass-through/interference prohibition; solids/viscous pollutants that obstruct a POTW; local specific limits and BMPs in the circumstances described.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies within the U.S. POTW pretreatment framework, with local authority and site-specific conditions. No location or receiving authority is supplied.
sources.applicability: Illustrates why the actual local control authority must decide; does not conclude that this synthetic workshop is a regulated industrial user or that any particular discharge is allowed.

sources.title: U.S. EPA Pretreatment Standards and Requirements—Local Limits
sources.version_or_release: Current web page; no page revision date displayed.
sources.locator: Page sections on pretreatment standards, local-limit purpose, site-specific nature, and local limits at industrial-user end-of-pipe.
sources.observed_operation: Explains that local limits may be numeric or narrative and protect a POTW, receiving waters, workers, and sludge practices.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: U.S. POTW explanatory context; limits depend on the actual POTW/control authority.
sources.applicability: Supports partner inquiry only; no local rule or discharge permit is known.

sources.title: eCFR 40 CFR §262.11 — Hazardous waste determination and recordkeeping
sources.version_or_release: Current eCFR page as of 2026-10-07; page states Title 40 last amended 2026-10-02.
sources.observed_operation: Calls for accurate solid-waste determination at generation before dilution/mixing/alteration and uses process/composition knowledge and testing for listings/characteristics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: U.S. RCRA rules; applicability and any more stringent local/state rules are unknown here.
sources.applicability: Shows why composition and process history matter before assigning solids or liquid a route; not a finding that any workshop waste is hazardous.

sources.title: GE/Housatonic River Site QAPP Vol. 2, Appendix A-3, laboratory SOP for EPA Method 160.2
sources.version_or_release: QAPP October 1998; included Method 160.2 SOP Revision 4.0 dated 1997-09-04.
sources.locator: Appendix A-3, PDF pp. 14–18; Scope, summary, sample handling, and QC.
sources.observed_operation: TSS/non-filterable residue is quantified gravimetrically from material retained on glass-fiber filter; SOP describes water/industrial waste scope and QC.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Dated, site/lab SOP; filter and handling details affect results. It is not a universal protocol for the workshop.
sources.applicability: Supports proposed measurement of suspended solids; a qualified lab should pick the current matrix-appropriate method and QA/QC.

sources.title: U.S. EPA Method 200.8, Revision 5.4 — Trace Elements in Waters and Wastes by ICP-MS
sources.observed_operation: Defines separate operational preparation for dissolved (0.45 µm filtered) and total-recoverable (unfiltered) aqueous elemental analyses and laboratory QC.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Method selection, analytes, detection limits, matrix effects, and preservation depend on the question and qualified laboratory.
sources.applicability: Useful proposed distinction for later paired samples; no water or metal testing occurred.

sources.title: Helmut ROHDE GmbH Settling Tank TA 85 product page
sources.version_or_release: Current manufacturer page; no revision ID displayed.
sources.locator: Product description, technical data table, and feature list.
sources.observed_operation: Lists three-chamber separator, internal volume 85 L, fill volume 70 L, dimensions, material, mobility, and removable partition.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Manufacturer description and specification; no independent performance data or dissolved-phase result.
sources.applicability: A real product for comparing footprint, capacity, and cleanout design; not an endorsement, permission, or treatment guarantee.

sources.title: ROHDE Instruction Manual Sedimentation Tank TA 85
sources.version_or_release: Official English file BA-TA85_202603-01_EN.pdf; March 2026 version identifier.
sources.observed_operation: Water passes through three calmed compartments; most suspended particles are said to settle. One sink only; sudden gushing flow including a full 20 L sink can overflow; regular cleanout; collected solids require a fate decision based on glaze contents/local disposal.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Manufacturer's model-specific operation/maintenance instructions; its sewer connection and residue guidance do not establish local authorization. No independent treatment validation.
sources.applicability: Useful for testing flow-pulse, capacity, maintenance, and residue questions in transferability review.

sources.title: DiamondCore Tools Cink and Mini Cink product comparison
sources.version_or_release: Current manufacturer product page; no revision ID displayed.
sources.locator: Cink 2 introduction and comparison chart for operation, filtration, power, maintenance, price.
sources.observed_operation: Describes Cink 2 as recirculating clay-water cleanup, with manufacturer-listed multi-stage 1 µm filtration, electric/GFCI pump, mobile buckets, and displayed product prices.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Sales-page claims only; dynamic pricing; read the manual S10 for explicit use exclusions.
sources.applicability: Candidate for a clay-only comparator after source segregation; its claims cannot establish dissolved removal, discharge quality, or suitability for glazes.

sources.title: DiamondCore Tools Cink 2 User Manual
sources.locator: Safety p. 3; operation p. 6; maintenance pp. 7–9; troubleshooting pp. 11–12.
sources.observed_operation: Specifies clean/water-soluble clay-material use, explicitly excludes glazes/chemicals/hazardous materials, forbids sewer/septic connection, and directs local-rule disposal of collected contents. Documents cloudiness under heavy continuous use, periodic settling/refresh, filter cleaning/replacement, reduced flow as pores clog, and seal/leak troubleshooting.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Manufacturer intended-use and maintenance instructions for Cink 2; not evidence the system treats glaze-bearing rinse water.
sources.applicability: Rules the Cink 2 out for mixed/unknown glaze water; only relevant to an authorized, reliably segregated clay-only stream.

sources.title: DiamondCore Tools Cink 2 product detail, cautions, and customer review page
sources.version_or_release: Current manufacturer page at retrieval; no release date or revision ID displayed.
sources.locator: Product description, specs, cautions, and customer review section.
sources.observed_operation: Manufacturer describes an updated Cink 2 with flexible nozzle, foot switch, bucket dollies/cabinet, extra filters; claims four-stage clay filtration to 1 µm; lists unit/shipping weights and dynamic regional shipping prices. One hosted review reports motor noise impaired classroom conversation and the reviewer was considering a quieter pump.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Manufacturer page and a single user-generated review; no dated engineering change log, noise measurement, verified defect, or documented fix. Page cautions say not intended for glaze capture or reuse and mixed clay types are not compatible for reuse.
sources.applicability: Adds feasibility, version/update, and one reported noise concern to the Cink 2 review; anecdote is not proof of a general defect or treatment result. The manual S10 remains controlling for intended-use limits.

sources.title: ROHDE Instruction Manual Sedimentation Tank TA 85, July 2025 release
sources.version_or_release: Official multilingual manual; filename release date 2025-07-29; English section begins after German section.
sources.locator: §2.1 technical characteristics; §2.4 three-compartment operation; English §3.3 one-sink/20 L warning; §6.2 use; §8.3 residue handling.
sources.observed_operation: Older version lists 85 L volume, 587×387×523 mm, 12 kg; it has the same one-sink and sudden-full-20-L-sink overflow warning as the March 2026 manual, and the same three-compartment settling/regular cleanout approach.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Version comparison shows the newer manual adds an explicit 70 L fill volume and presents dimensions/weight differently; no manual changelog establishes whether this is a physical design change or revised specification. Both versions document the 20 L pulse/overflow condition.
sources.applicability: Version-history evidence only; confirm exact model/serial, usable capacity, and installation constraints with manufacturer before any future sizing. Neither version provides independent water-quality validation or local discharge permission.
